Control your Drayton Wiser heating from Gladys: rooms, hot water, smart plugs,
radiator valves and room thermostats. The integration talks to your **Wiser
HeatHub directly on your local network**: no Wiser cloud account, nothing goes
out to the internet, and it keeps working when your internet connection is
down.

## What you get

After the configuration, the **Discovery** tab lists:

- **Wiser HeatHub** — away mode, eco mode, and whether the boiler is heating.
- **One device per room** — temperature, humidity (when a Room Thermostat
  serves the room), target temperature, mode (**Off**, **Manual**,
  **Schedule**), heating state, **Boost** and window (when a radiator valve
  detects it).
- **Hot water** (when the hub drives a cylinder) — mode (**Off**, **On**,
  **Schedule**), heating state and **Boost**.
- **Smart plugs** — on/off, power (W) and energy (kWh).
- **Radiator valves** and **room thermostats** — battery, radio signal and, for
  a valve, the temperature next to the radiator.

How the controls behave, like in the Wiser app:

- a **target temperature** set while the room follows its schedule lasts until
  the next slot of the schedule; in Manual mode it stays;
- **Boost** adds a few degrees (2 °C by default) to the current temperature for
  a while (1 hour by default);
- **Away mode** drops every room to the away temperature set in the Wiser app.

## Before you start

You need two things: the **address** of the hub and its **secret**.

### 1. The hub address

Find the HeatHub in your router (its name starts with `WiserHeat`) and note its
IP address. Give it a **fixed address** (DHCP reservation) so it does not change.

### 2. The hub secret

The secret is a long key the hub only shows in setup mode. It does not stop the
hub from working: your heating keeps running during these steps.

1. Press the **setup button** on the hub once (on the back or side, depending on
   the model). Its light starts flashing.
2. With a phone or a computer, join the Wi-Fi network named **WiserHeatXXXXXX**
   that the hub opens.
3. Open [http://192.168.8.1/secret](http://192.168.8.1/secret) in a browser: copy the long text shown (it
   often ends with `==`).
4. Press the setup button again (or wait a few minutes) so the hub leaves setup
   mode, and reconnect your device to your home Wi-Fi.

The secret stays the same afterwards; you only need to read it again if you
reset the hub.

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Fill in **HeatHub address** and **HeatHub secret**.
3. Leave **Connection** on **Automatic**: recent second-generation hubs only
   answer HTTPS, the integration finds out by itself.
4. Optionally change the **refresh interval** (60 seconds by default: one read
   covers every room and device), the **boost** (degrees and duration) and the
   **hot water boost** duration.
5. Save, then click **Test the connection**: the answer shows the hub firmware,
   the number of rooms and devices.
6. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices you want.

## Actions

- **Test the connection** — reads the hub now and says what it serves, or what
  to fix (wrong address, refused secret…).
- **Identify a device** — pick a device: its LEDs blink. Pick a room and every
  valve and thermostat of the room blinks.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor (Gladys 5.1 or later),
in the **Integrations** category.

Triggers:

- **Window opened or closed** — a radiator valve detected an open window (a
  sudden drop in temperature) or its closing. Variables: `room`, `state`
  (`open` / `closed`).
- **Away mode changed** — away mode was turned on or off **outside Gladys**
  (Wiser app, hub button). Variable: `state` (`on` / `off`).
- **Battery low** — a valve or a thermostat needs new batteries soon.
  Variables: `device_name`, `room`, `level`, `battery` (%).
- **HeatHub connection lost or restored** — the hub stopped answering (power
  cut, Wi-Fi, wrong secret) or answers again. Variables: `state` (`lost` /
  `restored`), `reason`.

Actions (each one returns a result the following actions can test):

- **Boost a room** — degrees and duration; leave the room empty to boost every
  room.
- **Set a room temperature** — a duration of 0 lasts until the next slot of the
  schedule.
- **Back to the schedule** — cancels boosts and temporary temperatures of a
  room, or of every room.
- **Set away mode** — on or off.
- **Boost hot water** — for a number of minutes.

## Dashboard

- **Wiser heating** — every room at a glance (temperature, target, mode, and a
  badge: heating, boost, window open, off), the hub connection, away and eco
  modes, the boiler, hot water and batteries. Buttons: away mode, back to the
  schedule, hot water boost.
- **Wiser room** — pick a room in the widget settings: live temperature, target
  and humidity, mode, heating, boost and window. Buttons: **Boost** (asks the
  degrees and the duration), **Cancel override**, **Follow schedule**.

## Troubleshooting

- **"The HeatHub refused the secret"** — read the secret again (see above); it
  changes when the hub is reset.
- **"The HeatHub does not answer"** — check the address (it may have changed
  without a DHCP reservation) and that the hub is powered. The integration
  reports the hub as lost after two failed reads in a row, not at the first
  slow answer.
- **No humidity or window feature** — they only exist when the room has a Room
  Thermostat (humidity) or radiator valves (window).
- Heating actuators, underfloor heating controllers, lights and shutters of the
  Wiser range are not supported yet.
- Detailed logs: view the integration logs from Gladys (or `docker logs` on the
  host).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Drayton Wiser Heating asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration talks to your Wiser HeatHub directly on your local network, without the Wiser cloud. It needs the hub address (find it in your router) and the hub secret: press the setup button of the hub, join its WiserHeat Wi-Fi network and open http:\/\/192.168.8.1/secret. The documentation explains each step. |
| HeatHub address | `string` | Yes | IP address or host name of the hub on your network. Give it a fixed address in your router. |
| HeatHub secret | `secret` | Yes | The long key read at http:\/\/192.168.8.1/secret while connected to the hub in setup mode. |
| Connection | `select` | No | Automatic suits every hub: recent second-generation hubs only answer HTTPS. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the hub is read, in seconds. One read covers every room and device. |
| Boost (°C) | `number` | No | Degrees a room boost adds to the current temperature. |
| Boost duration (min) | `number` | No | How long a room boost lasts, in minutes. |
| Hot water boost (min) | `number` | No | How long a hot water boost lasts, in minutes. |

## How to install Drayton Wiser Heating in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Drayton Wiser Heating appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-draytonwiserheating:0.0.2`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-draytonwiserheating](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-draytonwiserheating).

Drayton Wiser Heating requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
